content:
The [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Format messy or minified HTML into clean, indented markup. Enter your HTML code and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like. Format messy or minified HTML into clean markup with two-space indentation: block elements nested properly, inline elements kept on the text line so sentences are not broken apart. Paste HTML from a page, a template or an email and get readable markup back in one click. Everything runs in your browser — your code is never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. ## How to use the HTML Beautifier Start by typing or pasting your HTML code. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order. 1. Paste your HTML into the editor (or use the sample). 2. Click Beautify — the formatted markup appears below. 3. Copy it and paste it into your project. ## How it works The [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result. ## Worked example Here is a typical example. Beautifying `

Hello

Text

` puts the div, the heading and the paragraph on separate indented lines. Try the same figures in the [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change. ## Trying it out The fastest way to see what the [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked. ## How it indents Block elements (div, section, ul, table and friends) open a new indented line; inline elements (a, strong, em, span, code) stay on the same line as the surrounding text so sentences are not split. Void elements such as img, br and input are left as they are, and comments and the doctype get their own lines. ## What it does not do It does not validate your HTML, close unclosed tags, or change attributes and text. Broken markup stays broken, just easier to read — run it through a validator if the page misbehaves. ## Tips A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself: - Beautify a minified page source to understand its structure before editing it. - Inline elements stay inline, so text with links and bold words is not split across lines. - Copy the result straight into your editor — the indentation is two spaces throughout. Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in. ## Frequently asked questions ### What does an HTML beautifier do? It re-formats HTML with consistent indentation — block elements nested on their own lines — so compressed or messy markup becomes readable. Try it with your own numbers in the [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds. ### Does it change my HTML? No. Only the layout changes: indentation and line breaks. Tags, attributes and text stay exactly as written. Try it with your own numbers in the [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds. ### Is my HTML uploaded anywhere? No. Formatting runs entirely in your browser. Try it with your own numbers in the [HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds. ### What do I need to use the HTML Beautifier? Just HTML code. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly. ## Related tools If this calculation is part of a bigger job, the other Text Tools tools on CalcHub can help. The [Word Counter](/word-counter), [Character Counter](/character-counter), [Reading Time Calculator](/reading-time-calculator) and [Remove Spaces](/remove-spaces) all work the same way — enter your values and the result appears instantly, free and with no sign-up. For more detail, read the guides to the [Word Counter](/blog/word-counter-guide) and [Character Counter](/blog/character-counter-guide), which explain how those calculations work and when to use them. ## Try it now - [Open the HTML Beautifier](/html-beautifier) - [Word Counter](/word-counter) - [Character Counter](/character-counter) - [Reading Time Calculator](/reading-time-calculator) - [Remove Spaces](/remove-spaces) - [Browse all Text Tools tools](/tools?category=Text%20Tools) - [More guides](/blog)
